item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-22
item.description: One document settles this morning, and it is the one that calls itself open. On 2026-11-20, at the 5G+Industrial Internet Conference in Wuhan, CAICT's industrial-internet institute director Jin Jian presented the agent identity and identity system as AI's key infrastructure, with four named principles — demand-pull, open compatibility, peer mutual recognition, interoperability — a management centre that decides which credential issuers to trust, distributed trusted-interconnection centres in Beijing, Xiamen, Chongqing and Wuhan, and an open-source project called OpenAgenet (OAN) offered to industry as the technical reference. OAN is real, it is public, and it is measurable: twenty repositories, sixteen of them its own, four hundred and eighty-eight commits since May, and every one of them from a single email address. The white paper's author is a CAICT researcher, and the governance model it specifies is a Root that issues the infrastructure credentials and a chain that records who is allowed to operate. The architecture document of the year's most consequential identity system is open. The commits are not. Alongside it: DeepSeek closed a CNY 100 billion second round on 2026-11-17, in which thirty-one external investors hold 17.27 per cent through a partnership platform, get five-year lock-ups and no voting rights, while CITIC Securities sits on both sides of the table as investor and listing sponsor. Two documents, one question — who is inside the perimeter, and who was let in to look.
